## What

Bounded dependency verification can save correct checksum receipts yet make no new durable progress. Both a COPY comparator and the final retained verifier formerly restarted at batch zero. Repeated donor ctime changes invalidated that prefix, so each pass spent its budget rechecking it before reaching later entries.

## Why it matters

A per-attempt counter is not evidence of new durable work. On EI-29332933823385863, the original preparation returned incomplete after donor-only ctime invalidation with unchanged saved comparison ranges. A native pre-fix regression reproduced this separately in COPY verification and fresh-process retained verification (testing:runs 24120671). The earlier 249 passing exact-ref staging cases proved independent staging bytes; they did not prove the original fair-progress requirement. That broader completion claim was retracted and the issue reopened.

Ctime drift alone identifies neither the writer nor a content mutation. Hardlink creation/removal in a fixture reproduces ctime-only drift, but the actor behind the original run remains unknown.

## How to apply

Keep a checksum-protected private scheduling cursor beside the existing proof journal. Advance it before attempting an untrusted batch so interruptions and process death preserve the next position. Visit the suffix then the prefix on resume, with no skipped population. In the retained verifier, stream the census rather than loading the entire population into memory.

The cursor controls ordering only. It never authorizes byte reuse or readiness. Every reused receipt still needs its exact binding, metadata, proof-vector and racy-window checks. COPY completion still requires whole-chunk recapture; final publication still requires complete source/destination byte and census checks. A changed binding resets the starting position and does not grant proof.

Test repeated actual metadata changes, not just a single successful retry: invalidate earlier donor metadata each pass, interrupt a later batch, preserve prior proof, and show later decisive batches are reached. Repeat in fresh OS processes, permute fixture creation order, cover N-1/N/N+1 around a batch boundary, and reject same-length/same-mtime corruption after the boundary. Native post-fix run24120672 measured six passing progress cases at batch sizes7/8/9; final expanded regression and type verification are tracked on the issue.
